request: Analyze GSE120862 for the paper (Contractile activity-specific transcriptome response to acute endurance exercise and training in human skeletal muscle.): how exercise affects gene expression as the paper intends.

final.primary_estimand: Contractile-activity-specific transcriptome response: exercised (Ex) vs contralateral non-exercised (NE) vastus lateralis at +1 h and +4 h after 60-min one-legged knee extension, within subject, in untrained and (after 2 mo aerobic training) trained state; secondary: training effect on baseline transcriptome (trained vs untrained baseline).
planned_contrasts: Ex vs NE at +1 h, untrained (abstract: 'DEGs between exercised and nonexercised muscle were evaluated at 1 and 4 h'; no count in abstract)
Ex vs NE at +4 h, untrained (same locator; no count in abstract)
Ex vs NE at +1 h, trained (GEO summary: 'in both untrained and trained skeletal muscle'; no count)
Ex vs NE at +4 h, trained (same; no count)
trained vs untrained at baseline (abstract: 'Transcriptome change at baseline after 2 mo of aerobic training'; no count)
final.inclusion: 7 untrained males, 84 samples = 7 subjects x 2 training states x 3 times x 2 legs (GEO overall design)
final.repeated_measure_unit: subject (all 12 conditions from each of 7 men)
final.normalization: DESeq normalization of HTSeq counts (GEO data_processing)
final.paper_method: DESeq family (GEO data_processing: HTSeq counts, 'Normalization of read counts provided by DESeq method'); exact DE model, pairing and threshold not stated in abstract

paper_threshold.source_locator: not in abstract; full text unavailable

final.paper_results: Abstract only: contractile-activity-specific responses were increases only (no decreased genes), regulated by CREB/ATF/AP1, MYC/MAX, E2F TFs; training-induced baseline changes (up and down) were more pronounced than acute contractile-specific responses and involved IRF/STAT TFs. GEO summary: contractile-specific responses in trained muscle substantially decreased relative to untrained.

paper_reconstruction.reasoning: Full text not available; reconstruction rests on the PubMed abstract (PMID 30779632) and GEO series description only. Factors and sample structure from GEO overall design and sample characteristics.

alignment.reasoning: Matrix columns are GSM ids (renamed from SRR in prep via recount3 metadata); exact match on metadata index. One 12-level cell factor grp = training x time x leg, plus subject.

matrix.reasoning: recount3 gene_sums are per-base coverage sums; prep divided by single-end read length (SRA read_info) and rounded, as recount3::compute_read_counts does. Integer fraction 1.0 after rounding. Paper input was HTSeq raw counts (GEO data_processing); the deposited GEO files (DESeq-normalized counts, FPKM) were unreachable.

design.subject: subject
design.reasoning: Paper's contractile-specific estimand is Ex vs NE leg at the same time point within subject (abstract). Training effect at baseline is trained vs untrained baseline; the abstract does not say whether legs were pooled, so it is run per leg (NE leg is the cleaner baseline: the Ex leg's baseline biopsy is 48 h after the prior bout). All from one model on 84 samples with subject blocking. Rejected: separate factors with interaction (paper describes cell-wise comparisons); pooling legs at baseline (unknown, would double-count subjects without a leg term).
